question: Does matching the walking actor to measured encoder coordinates improve deployment-consistent behavior, with the same checkpoint, reward, mechanics and training budget?

implementation.correction: The opt-in deployment_measured actor observes q+b-default. Commands retain u-b conversion. Fixed default/reference poses, constant-bias joint velocities, privileged critic state, sensor-noise draws and IMU latency are unchanged. Legacy simulation behavior remains explicitly reproducible.
implementation.export_metadata_scope: The encoder_observation_contract records the TRAINING actor convention. Hardware and common native deployment consume measured joint positions; a legacy_true tag is not a mechanism for hardware to obtain true joint angles.

training.iteration_convention: RSL performs 1000 updates with labels 8495 through 9494; 9495 is the exclusive loop bound. Actual optimizer counters advance 170000→190000, independently confirming the continued budget.

evaluation.holdout_scope: Seed 404 is the predeclared holdout for this study and was not used to select these arms. Other class studies have used this seed.
evaluation.stop_criterion: Body planar speed ≤ 0.02 m/s and absolute body yaw rate ≤ 0.05 rad/s for 26 observations at 50 Hz, spanning 0.5 s from first to last. A reset or timeout refuses success. This is a sampled base-speed measurement, not proof that every joint is still or that the physical robot will remain stopped.
evaluation.support_persistence: Separate 1% and 10% body-weight thresholds; consecutive observed sample spans greater than 1 s, excluding invalid/reset rows. Mean prior 20 ms physics-interval torso forces do not prove contact continuity between observations.
evaluation.slip_metric: Horizontal foot-site speed gated by foot contact; a proxy distinct from native contact-point slip.

decision.finding: Measured-sensing training improves the tail of the sampled base-speed stop criterion and slightly reduces moving mean support, effort and slip proxy. It slightly worsens XY/yaw tracking and increases idle mean support and persistent light support. The result does not establish general superiority or complete off-belly walking.
decision.native_boundary: The separate common-measured native comparison finds reduced moving torso support in four selected donor/material pairs, but directional tracking/slip tradeoffs and residual support remain. All eight adverse fixed-default tails fail both the original 2 s and extended 8 s quiet screens. Both nominal chains pass their scoped screen. The fixed default mass/inertia robustness issue is separate from this sensing correction.
decision.next_training: Use the explicit measured-sensing mode for new hardware-consistent training experiments. Keep legacy_true only when reproducing historical simulation semantics. No further optimization is launched from this comparison; physical calibration and supervised validation remain necessary.

future_training_recipe.continuation_requirement: The override is bound to the exact checkpoint SHA, requires an explicit mode, and records old training mode separately from active mode. Never substitute a smoke checkpoint for an approved study start. Retain all intended controller/driver/slew/mechanics settings from the existing recipe.
future_training_recipe.export_and_evaluation: Standalone export restores the tagged training mode. Evaluating a legacy-trained policy under deployment_measured requires the same explicit mode-change permission; both arms in this study were evaluated this way.

runtime_closure.status: Stopped successfully; subsequent CLI status reports session not found. No active workers or GPU compute processes were present immediately before release.

limitations: One training seed; correlated repeated commands are not independent hardware trials.
Seed 404 was predeclared for this study and not used to select these arms; it has been used in other class studies.
Torso force is the simulated mean over previous 20 ms interval; observed loaded sample spans do not prove between-sample continuity.
Foot-site velocity gated by foot contact is a slip proxy, not actual contact-point slip.
Nominal-mechanics companion retains sensor noise, latency and reset randomness.
Sampled target limits/rates do not establish all substeps or hardware compliance.
Fixed default fallback stopping and torso-support failures in native startup transfer remain separate; no automatic promotion or installation.
